creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 12, item 5 (a +1 on an earlier report).

```rad
fn f():
    x = 1
    defer:
        print("deferred", x)
    print("in f")

f()
print("after f")
```

On main this prints `in f`, `after f`, then `error[RAD20028]: Undefined variable: x`. `rad check` is clean. In the real script a helper made a temp dir and registered its cleanup with `defer:`; the cleanup ran at script exit, failed, and left the dir behind. The syntax reference shows only script-level `defer`.

Either run a function's defers when the function returns, in its scope, or reject `defer` inside a function with a diagnostic.

Where: `core/interpreter.go:421` appends every defer to the script-wide `i.deferBlocks` with only its body, no env.
title: defer inside a function runs at script exit and cannot see the function's locals
